cards.explanation: The answer is that Jesus heals him so he can speak and see. Right there in front of everybody, Jesus heals the man so that he can speak and see. Two problems, one healing, no waiting. I think that man's first look at the crowd must have been something, friends. Imagine being able to see and speak in the same moment.

The answer is that they ask if He could be the Son of David. The crowds were astounded and asked, "Could this be the Son of David?" They saw a man healed so that he could speak and see, and a big question came out of their mouths. Notice it's a question, not an announcement, friends. I think they were still picking their jaws up off the floor.

The answer is False. The Pharisees, strict religious leaders, say, "Only by Beelzebul, the prince of demons, does this man drive out demons." The crowds were wondering about the Son of David, and these leaders went a totally different direction. Same healing, two very different reactions, friends.

The answer is that it will be laid waste. Jesus says, "Every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste…" A kingdom that fights itself is in real trouble, friends. I've seen two cookie cutters argue over the same spot on the dough, and nobody wins that one. Jesus adds that the same goes for any city or household.

The answer is that his kingdom could not stand. Jesus asks, "If Satan drives out Satan, he is divided against himself. How then can his kingdom stand?" His point is that a kingdom pulling against itself can't hold together. It's like a team where everybody pushes the other way, bakers.

The answer is judges. Jesus says, "So then, they will be your judges." He asks the Pharisees by whom their own sons drive out demons, if He does it by Beelzebul. Those sons are the Pharisees' own, and Jesus puts them right in the middle of the question. I'd feel that one all the way down to my gold base, friends.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "But if I drive out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you." That's the other option, set right beside the Pharisees' claim. Two choices, friends, and He says what the second one means.

The answer is tie up. Jesus says no one can plunder a strong man's house "…unless he first ties up the strong man?" Only then can he plunder the house. First the strong man, then the house. Order matters, friends, same as dough before oven.

The answers are against and scatters. Jesus says, "He who is not with Me is against Me…" There's no middle seat in that sentence, bakers. It's said plainly, and you can't miss it. Jesus says, "…he who does not gather with Me scatters." Gathering and scattering are opposites, and He puts them side by side. Think of crumbs: gather them up or they go everywhere. I've swept up plenty of those.

The answer is blasphemy against the Spirit. Jesus says, "…every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven men, but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven." That's a heavy line, friends. Notice how wide the first half is: every sin and blasphemy. Only this one is named as the exception.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven…" He then says whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven. Two different lines, friends, and He keeps them apart.

The answer is by the fruit it grows. Jesus says, "…a tree is known by its fruit." You don't judge a tree by how it looks from far away, friends. You look at what it makes. Same as my cookies: the proof is in the batch.

The answer is the overflow of the heart. Jesus says, "…out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks." Think of a bowl filled right to the top, friends. What's inside spills out the sides. The mouth just shows what's already in there.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "…the evil man brings evil things out of his evil store of treasure." Right before that, He says the good man brings good things out of his good store. A person brings out what's stored up, friends. That's a good reminder to watch what we pack in.

The answer is careless. Jesus says, "…men will give an account on the day of judgment for every careless word they have spoken." Every careless word, friends, not just the big speeches. I talk a lot, so I'm taking that one seriously.

The answer is acquitted. Jesus says, "…by your words you will be acquitted, and by your words you will be condemned." Acquitted means cleared. Our words matter either way, friends. That's a good reason to be thoughtful about what comes out.
